title: KV interleaved slice mapping and cross-stage prefetch protocol for multi-GPU runtime
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: As model sequence lengths and concurrent stream counts grow, our current KV placement strategies create hotspots and unpredictable OOMs across tensor/pipeline parallel boundaries. Goal: design a memory-efficient, low-latency KV mapping and prefetch protocol that shards KV memory into small deterministic slices and coordinates placement and prefetching across tensor-parallel ranks and pipeline stages. This ticket defines the 'KV interleaved slice mapping' concept, runtime protocol for cross-stage prefetch, correctness/consistency rules, fallback policies, and benchmarks for rollout. Constraints: must work with existing pipeline-stage checkpoints, respect KV eviction policies, be compatible with mixed-precision and 4-bit quantized caches, and add minimal control-plane overhead.
problem_statement: Current large-slab KV sharding ties contiguous token prefixes to single devices for simplicity. That causes uneven memory utilization when attention lengths vary between requests and when pipeline stages are imbalanced. We see token-level OOM bursts under high-concurrency serving and degraded tail latency when a single stage is forced to service multiple hot prefixes. We need a fine-grained mapping that evens utilization and enables stage-local prefetch to avoid remote fetch latency spikes.
proposal_summary: Introduce KV slice mapping: split each layer's KV store into fixed-size slices (configurable slice_bytes). Use a deterministic interleaving function to assign slices across the tensor-parallel ranks and pipeline stages such that adjacent tokens distribute across devices. Implement a lightweight cross-stage prefetch protocol: ahead-of-time prefetch hints are emitted by the scheduler based on sequence prefix predictions and batch-level token distributions. Prefetches are coordinated with an LRU-aware soft-reservation so slices can be pulled into a stage without violating memory SLOs. Fallback: if prefetch fails or memory budget is tight, gracefully degrade to localized on-demand fetches with bounded retry/backoff and an early response mode that triggers model fallback variants.
design_decisions: Use slice granularity between 8KB-64KB (tunable per-model) to balance control overhead vs fragmentation
Deterministic XOR-interleave function for mapping slices to (tensor-rank, pipeline-stage) pair to avoid metadata lookups
Keep a compact slice directory stored in host memory and optionally replicated to stage-local pinned memory for fast lookup
Prefetch hints generated by runtime scheduler based on the batch's token prefix histogram and the model's kv-access trace profile
Eviction respects a per-stage soft-reservation so prefetch doesn't cause hard OOMs; eviction is cooperative across ranks via a simple lease protocol
Compatibility shim for existing KV serialization format so on-disk checkpoints remain readable
implementation_plan: 1) Add slice metadata and deterministic mapping function to runtime core (C++): create compact directory format and APIs
2) Implement per-stage slice cache with LRU + soft-reservation semantics in serving runtime
3) Scheduler: extend batching planner to emit prefetch hints and a bounded prefetch budget per request
4) Cross-stage prefetch protocol: implement lease/ack messages over the existing control-plane RPC channel
5) Implement fallback: on prefetch miss, do async fetch with backpressure and request-level timeout
6) Integration tests with TPxPP topologies (TP=1..8, PP=1..16) and mixed-precision KV encodings
7) Load tests on dedicated-repro cluster and perf regression dashboarding
8) Gradual rollout plan: start with non-critical model group under canary routing, then expand
acceptance_criteria: 1) No functional regressions in KV serialization/deserialization across formats
2) Tail latency (p95/p99) under 100 concurrent long-sequence streams improves or stays equal compared to baseline on at least 3 tested model sizes
3) Max per-device KV memory utilization variance across devices reduced by >=30% on representative workloads
4) Prefetch protocol does not introduce >2% CPU overhead on the control plane at production load
5) Rollout in canary results show zero increased error-rate and memory-related crashes
6) Comprehensive unit/integration tests and a new perf dashboard with slice-level telemetry shipped
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete. Measured token-access entropy on three production workloads — found hotspots at token offsets corresponding to long system prompts.
2026-03-04: Prototype mapping function implemented (xor-interleave). Microbenchmarks show directory lookup < 80ns on host and < 200ns when stored in pinned stage-local mem.
2026-03-06: Design review with infra and serving runtime — agreed on slice size defaults and lease semantics; raised concern about control-plane RPC saturation for aggressive prefetching.
2026-03-08: Scheduler prototype patched into batching planner; end-to-end smoke test on 4xA100 (TP=2, PP=2) passes correctness for simple streams.
2026-03-10: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2741 with core mapping and per-stage cache; initial CI failing on mixed-precision serialization edge-case.
2026-03-12: Fixed serialization edge-case and added additional integration test for quantized KV.
open_questions: What is the best default slice_bytes per model family? (we need an automated heuristic)
Should the slice directory be sharded across host CPUs for extreme-concurrency servers?
How do we measure and expose slice fragmentation to SRE in the console?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Increased fragmentation leading to wasted memory. Mitigation: implement compaction job that can re-map contiguous slices during low utilization windows.
Risk: Control-plane overhead from prefetch hints. Mitigation: budget prefetches per batch and fall back to sampling-based hinting.
Risk: Cross-stage lease races causing transient double-alloc. Mitigation: use short lease TTL + idempotent allocation path and conservative retry logic.
testing_plan: Unit tests for mapping function, lease protocol, and eviction semantics
Integration tests across TP/PP configurations using our canary cluster
Perf tests: compare baseline vs slice mapping on seq-len 4096 and concurrent streams 1..128
Chaos tests: simulate OOM on one stage and verify controlled fallback and no request-level crash
review_feedback: PM (Jade Morales): prioritize stability over aggressive prefetching; require conservative default budgets
Infra (Diego Ramos): prefer directory in host-pinned memory to avoid GPU page faults on initial lookup
SRE (Maya Singh): add observability hooks for slice-level eviction and lease contention
